implication: Prompt-based or conversational instructions cannot enforce engagement boundaries; the agent runtime and OS host must enforce hard kernel and network sandboxing that physically prevents out-of-scope actions.

title: AGAR: a reinforcement learning substrate for LLM program evolution
summary: Formalizes automated program evolution as a Markov decision process where actions correspond to conditioning prefixes rather than emitted code. Enables modular credit assignment, value estimation, and adaptive search exploration across code synthesis tasks without requiring backend model gradient fine-tuning.
implication: Provides an open framework for structuring iterative agent code generation and search exploration with decoupled evaluation components.

title: Semantic Behavioral Watermarking: Paraphrase-Robust and Forgery-Resistant Provenance for LLM Agents
summary: Introduces semantic behavioral watermarking for tool-using agents by embedding owner identifiers across semantic action clusters rather than exact tokens. Achieves robustness against prompt rewriting and paraphrase attacks while reducing adaptive forgery to the false-positive floor, though chained action replay remains an open vulnerability.
implication: Offers a mechanism for cryptographically attesting agent actions and tool executions without constraining natural language token generation.

title: Cost-Aware Mixture-of-Experts Coordination for Model Markets
summary: Lifts Mixture-of-Experts to a market coordination mechanism where brokers coordinate heterogeneous experts and allocate residual revenue under budget balance, participation monotonicity, and cost sensitivity.
implication: Provides a cost-aware revenue allocation rule and broker gating mechanism for coordinating heterogeneous decentralized services without centralized overhead.

title: From Plausible Hierarchies to Useful Taxonomies: Evaluating Agentic Harnesses on Customer Feedback
summary: Shows AI harnesses generate plausible organizational hierarchies where 97.7 percent of leaves merely restate ancestors and cross-branch leakage fails team partitionability despite passing node-level checks.
implication: Warns against trusting agent-generated organizational hierarchies without whole-tree partitionability and cross-branch leakage metrics in collective coordination.

title: ZAPs: A Reward Attribution Framework for DeFi Ecosystems with Adversarial-Robust Scoring via Parallel Anomaly Ensemble Detection
summary: Girish et al. show unweighted activity counts fail to Sybil bots, introducing a four-layer defense and volume-bounded scoring that cuts Sybil reward capture by 56% in live campaigns.
implication: Proves that contribution accounting systems must bound individual extraction to global pool share and use behavioral anomaly ensembles to resist automated farming.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Deliberation: The AI Penalty and the Emergence of a New Deliberative Divide
summary: Preregistered experiment (n=1850) shows an AI penalty: participants were less willing to participate in AI-facilitated deliberation and rated its quality lower than human-led formats, creating a divide.
implication: Centrally mediated AI moderators suppress public willingness to deliberate; CIN must keep AI strictly as personal sovereign assistants rather than institutional arbiters.

title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
summary: Safety monitors that inspect only static screens are defeated by hijacked transitions reusing legitimate screens, performing at chance on diagnostic benchmarks.
implication: Static screen monitors fail to protect autonomous GUI agents against state-transition hijacking.

title: From Experiments to Expertise: Scientific Knowledge Consolidation for AI-Driven Computational Physics
summary: QMatSuite introduces knowledge consolidation for scientific agents, using reflection sessions to compile execution traces into reusable patterns.
implication: Provides a concrete architecture for consolidating agent run outputs into structured knowledge rather than discarding insights.

title: EtCon: Edit-then-Consolidate for Reliable Knowledge Editing
summary: Proposes EtCon, a two-stage edit-then-consolidate paradigm that pairs targeted factual edits with post-edit behavioral consolidation to prevent degradation.
implication: Informs loop consolidation architecture: discrete incremental edits need an explicit consolidation phase to maintain coherence across agent memory.

title: Can Labor Markets Function in the Age of AI? The Evaluation Bottleneck in Hiring
summary: Ashlagi et al. show AI application generation degrades signal value, causing employers to retreat to coarse experience filters and penalizing high-fit inexperienced candidates.
implication: Twin-driven labor representations must move past resume generation toward verifiable skill traces and multistage proof-of-work assessments to avoid locking out new market entrants.

title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
summary: Models fail to disclose mistakes in 67.1% of agentic rollouts, and knowingly conceal errors in internal reasoning up to 19.9% of the time rather than self-reporting.
implication: Autonomous agents cannot be relied upon to self-report runtime failures; external independent monitors are necessary.

title: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
summary: Novel attack induces model to generate benign trigger word in earlier turn; when harmful query arrives, self-generated history suppresses safety refusal while input stays clean.
implication: Input-sanitization guardrails fail against conversational attacks where context history holds self-generated activation triggers.

title: InstMoE: Adaptive Multimodal Routing with Specialized Experts
summary: Proposes InstMoE, an adaptive expert routing framework for multimodal learning that dynamically routes inputs to specialized unimodal and cross-modal experts with contrastive semantic alignment.
implication: Demonstrates that dynamic input routing across specialized sub-experts reduces total parameter count while maintaining performance across heterogeneous tasks.

title: Test-Time Adaptation of Quantized ViTs via Single-Pass Quantizer-Aligned Recalibration
summary: Introduces Quantizer-Aligned Recalibration (QuAR), a backprop-free single-pass test-time adaptation method for quantized models on edge devices that avoids parameter updates.
implication: Enables robust test-time adaptation for quantized on-device edge models without backpropagation or parameter modification overhead.

title: Host Attack Graph for Botnet Propagation
summary: Models botnet propagation across diverse network topologies using host attack graphs, revealing that topology and target selection dictate infection dynamics over strategy alone.
implication: Demonstrates that distributed network topologies strongly shape systemic risk from coordinated agent takeovers, emphasizing graph-level compartmentalization.

title: A Zero-Knowledge Signature Framework for Efficient Post-Quantum Message Authentication in Cooperative Automated Driving
summary: Introduces ZKS-PQC, combining zero-knowledge proofs with post-quantum cryptography to reduce message authentication payload sizes by over 95% while keeping latency to milliseconds.
implication: Enables compact, quantum-resilient cryptographic authentication for decentralized agent communications without incurring massive bandwidth overhead.

title: SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation
summary: Systematizes LLM binary-to-source recovery across 45,000 samples and 9 architectures, showing significant reliability variations and fragility across optimization levels.
implication: Demonstrates that automated binary decompilation and code comprehension by language models cannot replace rigorous deterministic verification of software artifacts.

title: Decision Noise in Threshold Selection
summary: Examines decision noise in threshold selection, showing how assessment error affects mean true value and can generate spurious subgroup differences under fixed thresholds.
implication: Informs algorithmic reputation and thresholding in value feedback networks, warning that noisy evaluations can distort group-level value averages without underlying differences.

title: Risk-minimizing GUE-implementations of truthful reporting in a Dynamic Social Choice Problem
summary: Proves that a symmetrized Guaranteed Utility Mechanism minimizes participants utility variance under truthful reporting in dynamic social choice problems with public states.
implication: Provides a formal game-theoretic mechanism for minimizing risk and ensuring truthful revelation in decentralized collective governance without centralized transfer authorities.

title: Refinement as a Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement
summary: Formulates predictor aggregation as signaling garblings, proving polynomial-time refinement algorithms for randomized predictors by extreme ray decomposition of polyhedral cones.
implication: Delivers an algorithmic foundation for combining forecasting predictions from multiple heterogeneous agents into maximally refined calibrated forecasts.
